title: Training Note: Basket Size and the Wrong-Item Refund on Cartwise Grocery Orders
content:
**Training note — Cartwise Grocery Orders wrong-item refunds and basket size.** The size of the order raises a wrong-item refund in the terms below.

**What raises the refund?**
The wrong-item basket uplift raises the refund after the share is applied: when the order's item subtotal (the sum of its billed item lines) is **at least 50.00** and the order has **at least 5 billed item lines**, the refund is raised by **5 percent**; when the item subtotal is at least 50.00 and the order has **fewer than 5** billed item lines, it is raised by **2 percent**; otherwise it is not raised.

**Where does the raise sit in the figure?**
The wrong-item value times the share is multiplied by 1 plus the uplift percentage, and it is that raised product that is rounded to the cent — once, after the raise, not before it.

**What counts as a billed item line?**
Every billed item line entry on the order counts once, whatever its quantity; the item subtotal is the sum of those lines' billed amounts.

**Are 50.00 exactly and 5 lines exactly enough?**
Yes. Both conditions read "at least", so a subtotal of exactly 50.00 meets the first and exactly 5 lines meet the second.

**Summary**

| Item subtotal | Billed item lines | Raise |
|---|---|---|
| 50.00 or more | 5 or more | 5 percent |
| 50.00 or more | 4 or fewer | 2 percent |
| below 50.00 | any number | none |

**Hypothetical figures.** Suppose the value times the share comes to 6.18 on an order of 7 lines totalling 88.40: raised by 5 percent it is 6.489, rounded to 6.49. On an order of 3 lines totalling 61.00 the same 6.18 is raised by 2 percent to 6.3036, rounded to 6.30. On an order totalling 49.99 it is not raised.
